_about: LGIC_ENFORCE round 8, cell EN-m-39 (TO LGIC_ENFORCE.TO-EN-m-39-r8). The mechanism distinguishing an S3 KEY TEMPLATE from an S3 KEY, landed as org/standards/NAMING_SCHEMA.json key.template_detection (v1.10 -> v1.11). This record is the Rule 24 four-postulate record + word-boundary token census R-62 requires for the schema act, plus the discrimination arm the order's own bar names.
author: 0.9.0_WK_LGIC_ENFORCE~3

schema_edit.nothing_else_touched: types_not_graded_by_kind, kind, grade, resource, secret, log_group, iam_policy and every other top-level block are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the round-8 cut; only 'version', 'changelog' (one appended entry) and 'key' (one new field) changed. Verified by loading both trees and diffing every OTHER top-level key's json.dumps() -- zero differences outside those three.

four_postulates.mece_over_a_declared_domain: DECLARED DOMAIN: every S3Key row a census can encounter, on either plane (repo or live), printed with its denominator by round 7's own unscoped read -- 1370 carried rows, brace-in-current run UNSCOPED (not just over the 235-row NON_SYSTEM_PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN class) returned 15 of 1370, all 15 inside the class and none outside it (LABEL_TRUTH_R7.json 'NEGATIVE CONTROL' block, W1-S70 evidence). The subtraction this field states -- KEY_TEMPLATE = {rows whose raw `current` carries a brace token outside the four grade.placeholder sanctions}; ORDINARY_KEY = DOMAIN minus KEY_TEMPLATE -- is a binary partition with ZERO third case: a row's `current` either carries an unsanctioned brace or it does not, so every S3Key row falls into exactly one side. Re-verified here on a SECOND corpus round 7 did not use (PLACEHOLDER_CAMPAIGN_R6.json's own 106 S3Key rows): 15 template + 91 ordinary = 106, remainder 0 (see discrimination block). The domain was falsified against the claim's own population before the subtraction was trusted, per Rule 24's own requirement, not merely asserted.
four_postulates.same_grain: The predicate runs at the ROW's raw, pre-grade `current` string -- never at the TYPE (S3Key as a whole, which is types_not_graded_by_kind's grain) and never at the GRADE's OUTPUT (canonical_form, a DIFFERENT object the grade computes downstream by OPENING placeholders). Conflating those grains is the exact defect round 7 named: 'the census graded a KEY TEMPLATE as if it were a key' -- treating a producer's own declared brace (present before any grade ran) as though it were a grade-opened gap. template_detection reads only the row's OWN declared bytes, at the same grain across the 15 templates, the 91 ordinary keys tested, and every other S3Key the schema will ever see.
four_postulates.intent_coherence: ONE axis: 'is this row's own declared name a format template or a name'. It is never conflated with 'should this TYPE be graded at all' (types_not_graded_by_kind's axis, untouched -- S3Key stays routed) or 'is this key's GRAMMAR correct' (grade()'s axis, key.grammar, untouched -- an ordinary key that fails key.grammar still grades OUT-OF-PATTERN exactly as before). template_detection answers its one question and defers every other question to the field that already owns it.
four_postulates.state_coherence: Values this remedy does NOT move, named: (1) types_not_graded_by_kind's 8/7 split -- measured unchanged below, deliberately_moved empty; (2) grade()'s verdict computation for any row -- no code file is touched (lib/opal_naming.py and .tools/naming-gate.py are UNEDITED; template_detection is pure schema DATA with no reader yet, so it is DESIRED, not APPLIED, per CLAUDE.md's value-must-carry-its-claim doctrine); (3) the 15 templates' own disposition -- they stay CARDED under ROW_IS_NOT_A_NAME, owner 2.0.0_SA_COO~G, exactly as R-62 (c) left them; (4) any live S3 key's actual conformance status -- NOTHING LIVE MOVES, per the order's own bound, and this field cannot move it because nothing reads it yet.

token_census.method: word-boundary regex (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])S3Key(?![A-Za-z0-9_]) applied to the FULL, UNTRUNCATED text of every file comp-find identified as containing the literal substring 'S3Key' (comp-find 'S3Key' --files --all, corpus=all), read directly via Python rather than parsed from comp-find's own display (which truncates long lines and would undercount). whole_value_hits = occurrences passing the word-boundary regex; substring_hits = ALL naive occurrences of the literal substring (a superset that INCLUDES the whole-value ones, by construction, which is why it is always >= whole_value_hits -- a substring read never finds fewer hits than a word-boundary read, only more, and the gap between the two IS the substring-inflation hazard this project was bitten by twice).
token_census.denominator_basis: total lines scanned across the 456 files comp-find's own sweep identified (its printed DENOMINATOR line: '10704 hit(s) across 35611 file(s) scanned in scope [corpus=all]'; 456 of those files actually carry the literal substring and were read in full)
token_census.reading: The gap (89 of 10860, 0.8%) is real and concentrated in identifier compounds (recognizer class names, a plural, a prefixed variable) -- exactly the shape 'C6 inside C33R6-AC6' and 'sentiment inside a quoted grep pattern' warned about. None of the 89 are S3Key VALUES (a node_type or a graded row's type field); every genuine (type == 'S3Key') census elsewhere in this project's own records reads the word-boundary count, which is why the mechanism this cell adds keys off the row's `current` field rather than off a substring search of any kind.

exclusion_table_after.measured_how: loaded org/standards/NAMING_SCHEMA.json AFTER this cell's edit, re-ran the exact switch at lib/opal_naming.py:1012 (`str(why).startswith('NOT GRADED')`) over types_not_graded_by_kind -- unchanged 8/7 split, S3Key still in still_routed (not moved into genuinely_not_graded). deliberately_moved is empty because nothing was moved.

discrimination.population_tested: PLACEHOLDER_CAMPAIGN_R6.json's 106 S3Key rows (a corpus round 7 did NOT use to derive the 15, so this is a genuinely independent negative-arm population), less the 15 template `current` values -- 91 remain.
discrimination.instrument: extract every {[^{}]+} brace token from each row's `current`; subtract {system},{source},{scope},{cadence}; non-empty remainder => template.
discrimination.positive_arm_result: 15 of the 15 known key_template_rows (LABEL_TRUTH_R7.json) return a non-empty remainder -- ALL correctly selected.
discrimination.negative_arm_result: 0 of the 91 ordinary S3Key rows return a non-empty remainder -- ALL correctly rejected. The tested denominator (91) is POSITIVE, per the order's own bar ('zero tested is a vacuous negative arm').
discrimination.note_on_silver_percent_s: 'silver/%s/' is REJECTED by this mechanism because it carries no BRACE token at all -- it uses a python %-format field, not a {} field, and round 7's own instrument (which this field promotes to data) is brace-only by its own explicit scope. See surprise row LGIC_ENFORCE-W3-S17: this is a genuinely different shape the brace-only mechanism does not reach, filed rather than silently folded into this cell's result.

not_done_here_and_why.no_code_reads_this_field_yet: template_detection is schema DATA only. Wiring lib/opal_naming.py or .tools/naming-gate.py to consult it is a DIFFERENT cell with a DIFFERENT <paths> grant (both files are outside this order's grant and outside the CLOUD_OPS_OR_ETL / infra lane this worker does not hold) -- NOTHING LIVE MOVES is the order's own bound, and it is honored by construction: no reader exists yet.
not_done_here_and_why.the_15_disposition_is_not_re_decided: Round 7 settled the 15's significance (ROW_IS_NOT_A_NAME, R-62 (c), owner 2.0.0_SA_COO~G). This cell adds the MECHANISM that would let a later census apply that disposition without a human re-deriving it row by row; it does not re-card, re-grade or re-own any of the 15.
